title: At the Scene of an Incident & First Aid
whatItIs: At an incident, make the scene safe, get help and give basic first aid. Knowing DR ABC can save a life.

keyFacts.text: In a collision causing damage or injury, you MUST stop. Give your details, or report it to the police within 24 hours.

keyFacts: Call 999 or 112 and give the exact location and the number of vehicles involved.
Don't move casualties who are still in vehicles unless there is further danger.
Don't remove a motorcyclist's helmet unless it is essential.
Don't give casualties anything to eat or drink. Keep them warm and reassure them.
Burns: cool with clean, cool water for at least 20 minutes.

visual.caption: DR ABC: first aid in order

items.title: D · Danger
items.text: Check for danger. Switch off engines, warn traffic, stop anyone smoking.

items.title: R · Response
items.text: Ask questions and gently shake their shoulders to get a response.

items.title: A · Airway
items.text: No response? Put your fingers under their chin and lift it forward to open the airway.

items.title: B · Breathing
items.text: Check for normal breathing. No signs of breathing? Start CPR: 5 to 6 cm deep, about twice a second.

items.title: C · Circulation
items.text: Responsive and breathing? Check for bleeding. Press firmly on the wound unless something is in it.

a.label: Burns
points: Cool with water for at least 20 minutes
Don't remove anything stuck to the burn

b.label: Bleeding
points: Something in it? Pad around it

onTheTest.question: An adult casualty is not breathing normally. How deep should chest compressions be?
onTheTest.why: Press hard and fast in the centre of the chest, 5 to 6 cm deep, at about twice a second.

traps: Burns: cool for at least 20 minutes with plenty of clean, cool water. Don't remove anything stuck to it.
Don't take off a motorcyclist's helmet unless it is essential.
Don't give a casualty anything to drink, not even water.

sources.ref: Rule 286 (If you are involved in a collision)
